teaser: Week 15: the 34-tool claims agent is losing accuracy, so you decompose it, defer tools on demand, audit privileges and gate risky actions.

scene.title: The 34-tool claims agent is drifting, and compliance wants to know who can issue refunds
scene.sceneHtml:
Pilot deployed, Week 15. The claims-processing agent has grown to 34 tools serving four distinct workflow domains. Tool-selection accuracy has fallen from 91% to 75%, and the engineering team reports that loading all 34 tool definitions consumes 22% of the context window on startup. Separately, the compliance officer asks: "Which tools can issue refunds or delete records? How do we ensure a procurement agent cannot approve its own purchase requests?"

Your task: decompose the bloated agent, apply progressive tool discovery to reduce context pressure, audit tool inventories for least privilege, and place human-in-the-loop (HITL) gates on high-consequence actions.

takeaways: Tool definitions from a big catalog or many MCP servers eating context: enable Tool Search (progressive discovery) so tools load on demand.
34 tools across four domains with overlapping descriptions: decompose into per-domain subagents and clean up tools before adding a router.
Least-privilege audit: remove tools outside the agent scope, tools granting excess permissions, and tools that bypass human approval gates.
Place HITL review between model output and high-impact irreversible actions (payments, deletions, external comms), not on every action.
